Senses.Explanation: “When tired, sleep” forms the second half of the hunger-and-sleep saying, and Dazhu’s case explicitly distinguishes this from sleeping while occupied by calculations. When tired, sleep. Its stable partner is ‘when hungry, eat’ . In the Jingde Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, the Vinaya master Youyuan asks Dazhu Huihai whether he exerts effort in following the Way. Dazhu says yes and answers with eating when hungry and sleeping when tired. When Youyuan objects that everyone does the same, Dazhu says they differ: while eating, others do not consent simply to eat but make a hundred demands; while sleeping, they do not consent simply to sleep but make a thousand calculations . A song attributed to Nanyue Lanzan places the pair after refusing delight in heaven or merit-making and before saying fools laugh while the wise understand. The words remain ordinary bodily actions; the recorded public exchange contrasts Dazhu’s stated exertion with the same-looking conduct accompanied by demands and calculation.
